clue.text: Topping wear in unusual red shades

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of red shades come in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Someone wears a hat in strange shades of red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the nine letters of RED SHADES. 'Topping wear' means something worn on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn on top of the head, such as a hat or a feathered band, is this.

clue.text: He deals with complaints in simple fashion

definitions.text: He deals with complaints in simple fashion

parts.words: He deals with complaints in simple fashion
parts.note: complaints are illnesses, and simples are old medicinal plants, so this is someone who treats ailments with plant remedies

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a customer services clerk; but 'complaints' are ailments and 'simples' are medicinal plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who grows or sells plants for medicine treats ailments with simples, old remedies made from single plants.

clue.text: A large number, all present

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
the sum is the whole amount, all of it

explanation.surface: A big crowd, with everybody in attendance.
explanation.walkthrough: ADSUM is Latin for 'I am here', the old reply at a school roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word is the reply 'I am here' at a roll call, meaning present.

clue.text: Upset caused by greed and corruption

indicators.note: corruption means the letters of greed and are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Distress brought about by avarice and dishonesty in public life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link but is part of the fodder: GREED AND is rearranged by 'corruption'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mentally disturbed or unhinged may be called upset in an old sense.

clue.text: All the same the cape makes a regular appearance

parts.note: things all the same are even, level or equal
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Every time, the same cloak turns up on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cape' looks like a garment; NESS is a headland, as in Dungeness on the Kent coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniformity, a smooth and level look with no irregularity, is the quality meant.

clue.text: Employees used to keep up standards

definitions.meaning: the people working for organisations are their workforces
standards are flags, held up on poles

explanation.definitionFit: Workforces are groups of employees, and poles hold up flags, which are called standards.

clue.text: The way a politician creates an impression

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way or road
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: How a politician makes an impression on the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creates an' is only a link between the wordplay and 'impression'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark pressed into wax or paper by a die is an impression, as on a seal.

clue.text: Ironic humour at being received by father

indicators.note: being received by means the word at goes inside the word for father

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A father receives a jibe of ironic wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockery using irony or ridicule, as in a lampoon, is this kind of humour.

clue.text: The hermit ate no rich pie

indicators.note: printers call a jumble of spilled type pie, so pie signals the letters of ate no rich are mixed up

explanation.surface: A hermit refused a rich pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like food; in printing, 'pie' is type that has been jumbled, so it rearranges ATE NO RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious recluse who lives alone, often walled in a cell, is a hermit.

clue.text: Drive, to get the newspapers …

definitions.meaning: newspapers taken together, journalism as a whole

explanation.walkthrough: The dots run on into 14 down in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive forward is to push on; newspapers and journalists together are known collectively by the same word.

clue.text: Book is in stock

definitions.meaning: to book a table or seat is to secure it in advance
a stock is a supply kept back for later use

explanation.definitionFit: To book is to set aside in advance; a stock is a supply kept back for future use: both senses of keeping something aside.

clue.text: This might be just the thing!

definitions.text: This might be just the thing!

parts.words: This might be just the thing!
parts.note: an item or thing can be called this, and the word 'the' is itself the definite one in grammar

explanation.walkthrough: Read as praise for something ideal; but an item is this, and 'the' is the definite one in grammar, so 'just the' points to it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an item or object and the grammar term for words like 'a' and 'the'.

clue.text: A fellow holding a thousand capital

indicators.note: holding means the word for fellow wraps round the thousand

parts.note: a fellow is a man
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A man clutching a thousand pounds of capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in the surface; it is a capital city, AMMAN in Jordan.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Jordan.

clue.text: Common-sense about putting out a fire in base

indicators.note: about tells us the word for common sense goes round the rest

parts.note: nous is common sense, practical intelligence

indicators.note: putting out reads as extinguishing, but it signals that the letters of a fire are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Using common sense to extinguish a fire at a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' looks like firefighting but is the anagram signal, giving EFARI from A FIRE. 'base' means low or wicked, not a camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the moral sense means low and wicked, which is what villainous behaviour is.

clue.text: Swell position for batsman

definitions.meaning: to swell is to grow larger
in cricket a batsman standing at the crease is in his safe ground

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line the batsman stands behind; 'in crease' is where he is safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger, as a number grows; a batsman behind the line is safely 'in crease'.

clue.text: Drive, to get the newspapers … to read with the family

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read
a strain is a line of descent, a family stock

explanation.surface: A pushy parent forces the family to sit down and read the papers together.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue continues 8 down, whose 'Drive' is the definition for both. CON is an old verb for studying a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or force someone to act is to compel them.

clue.text: The page badly needs medical treatment

parts.note: ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A page boy feels unwell and needs a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is not an anagram signal here; ILL means badly, as in 'ill-advised'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet swallowed as medicine is a common form of medical treatment.

clue.text: Subsequently a friend at one's side

parts.note: subsequently means later
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Later, a friend stands at someone's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways, from or towards one flank, is the sense.

clue.text: Don't forget about the constituent

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a member is a part or constituent of a whole

explanation.surface: A reminder not to forget about the voter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituent' suggests a voter writing to their MP; here it means a part, a member of a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep in mind, the opposite of letting something slip from the memory.

clue.text: Making contact can be emotive

explanation.definitionFit: Two things in physical contact meet; something moving that stirs the feelings is also described this way.

clue.text: Lean nurse

definitions.meaning: to lean towards something is to be inclined that way
to nurse someone is to look after them

explanation.definitionFit: To lean towards something is to be inclined that way; to nurse someone is to look after them: both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Torn about a gift, giving perfume

indicators.note: about tells us the word for torn wraps round the gift

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, meaning torn
a dole is a charitable gift or handout

explanation.surface: Someone rips the wrapping off a present and releases a scent.
explanation.walkthrough: Dole is an old word for a charitable handout, not just unemployment benefit; 'Torn' is the past participle rent, from rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fragrant, smelling strongly of a scent, is said to be this.

clue.text: One does not find fault with an amateur

parts.note: no can mean not, as in no better
a vice is a fault or failing

explanation.surface: A tolerant person refuses to criticise a beginner's efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One does ... find ... with an' only links: NO VICE, no fault, describes a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner or learner, someone new and inexperienced at a pursuit.

clue.text: In tears maybe, quietly gets to the point

indicators.note: In tells us the letter for quietly sits inside the jumbled tears
maybe suggests the letters of tears are a possible rearrangement

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A tearful person quietly comes to the heart of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges TEARS and 'In' places P, for piano, among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that narrows gradually to a sharp end is said to come to a point.

clue.text: To restrict alcoholic drink would be a reasonable solution - -

parts.note: to ration something is to restrict the amount allowed
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Rationing beer would be a sensible answer to a drinking problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots carry on into the next clue in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The reasoning behind a choice, its logical basis, is this.

clue.text: Some upstaged tragedians expressed real anger

indicators.note: some means only part of the words upstaged tragedians is taken

explanation.surface: Actors overshadowed by others on stage lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of the letters, here from tragedians.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormed or fumed, showing violent fury.

clue.text: … for singers knocking port back after church

indicators.note: after places the reversed port behind the church abbreviation
knocking back a drink is downing it, and together with back it tells us the port is turned round
back with knocking tells us the port is read from right to left

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Churchgoers who sing after downing glasses of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking ... back' looks like drinking port wine; it turns RIO, the port city, into OIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people who sing together, especially in a church, is this.

clue.text: Eight have to turn and the rest reverse in

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed rest goes inside the reversed to
turn tells us the word to is read backwards
reverse tells us the abbreviation for the rest is read backwards

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest

explanation.surface: Eight musicians must swap places while the others go back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' gives OT and 'reverse' gives CTE; 'Eight' at the front is the definition, though it reads as the subject of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight, especially eight musicians, is this.

clue.text: Stony, but in great form

definitions.note: used as an adjective, as in a granite face, the answer means hard and stony

indicators.note: form signals the letters of in great being shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A hard, stony appearance, yet the person is in fine fettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great form' looks like good health; 'form' rearranges IN GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard rock serves as an adjective for anything unyielding or hard as stone.

clue.text: City transport is to get cash

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway
taken as written
taken as written
L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Taking a train to the city to collect some money.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former UK railway, and L is the old sign for pounds sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A port in the west of England is a large city.

clue.text: The poet completed about a quarter

indicators.note: about tells us the word for completed goes round the quarter

parts.note: done means completed or finished
N is north, one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A poet finishing a quarter of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' is a compass point, N for north. John Donne was a 17th-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a metaphysical poet and Dean of St Paul's.

clue.text: Active Conservatives and the Left taken in by an agent

indicators.note: taken in by means the following parts sit inside the word for an agent

parts.note: an agent can be a spy
the Right is the conservative wing in politics
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Politicians of right and left are duped by a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled; here it is a container signal, and the Right is the political wing of Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and energetic, full of brisk movement, as an elderly but nimble person can be.
